source_text: Ἡ δὲ ἑσπερία θάλασσα τὰς ἀμπώτεις ὑφίσταται, νῦν μὲν ὑπονοστοῦσα, πάλιν δὲ ἐπικλύζουσα, ὥσπερ ἀναπνοαῖς τῆς σελήνης ὑφελκομένη πρὸς τὸ ὀπίσω, καὶ πάλιν ταῖς ἀπ' αὐτῆς ἐμπνοίαις, εἰς τὸ οἰκεῖον μέτρον προωθουμένη. Ταῦτά μοι εἴρηται πρὸς ἀπόδειξιν τοῦ κατὰ τοὺς φωστῆρας μεγέθους, καὶ σύστασιν τοῦ μηδὲ μέχρι συλλαβῆς ἀργόν τι εἶναι τῶν θεοπνεύστων ῥημάτων· καίτοι γε οὐδενὸς ἥψατο σχεδὸν τῶν καιρίων ὁ λό γος· πολλὰ γὰρ περὶ μεγεθῶν καὶ ἀποστημάτων ἡλίου καὶ σελήνης ἐστὶν ἐξευρεῖν τοῖς λογισμοῖς, τὸν μὴ παρέργως τὰς ἐνεργείας αὐτῶν καὶ τὰς δυνάμεις ἐπεσκεμμένον. Εὐγνωμόνως οὖν δεῖ κατηγορεῖν ἡμᾶς τῆς ἑαυτῶν ἀσθενείας, ἵνα μὴ τῷ ἡμετέρῳ λόγῳ μετρῆται τῶν δημιουργημάτων τὰ μέγιστα, ἀλλὰ ἐξ ὀλίγων τῶν εἰρημένων παρ' ἑαυτοῖς ἀναλογίζεσθαι, πόσα τινά ἐστι καὶ πηλίκα τὰ παρεθέντα. Μὴ τοίνυν μηδὲ σελήνην ὀφθαλμῷ μετρήσῃς, ἀλλὰ λογισμῷ, ὃς πολλῷ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ἀκριβέστερός ἐστι πρὸς ἀληθείας εὕρεσιν. Μῦθοί τινες καταγέλαστοι ὑπὸ γραϊδίων κωθωνιζο μένων παραληρούμενοι πανταχοῦ διεδόθησαν, ὅτι μαγγανείαις τισὶ τῆς οἰκείας ἕδρας ἀποκινηθεῖσα σελήνη πρὸς γῆν καταφέρεται. Πῶς μὲν οὖν κινήσει γοήτων ἐπαοιδὴ, ἣν αὐτὸς ἐθεμελίωσεν ὁ Ὕψιστος; Ποῖος δ' ἂν καὶ τόπος κατασπασθεῖσαν αὐτὴν ὑπεδέξατο; Βούλει ἀπὸ μικρῶν τεκμηρίων λαβεῖν τοῦ μεγέθους αὐτῆς τὴν ἀπόδειξιν; Αἱ κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην πόλεις πλεῖστον ἀλλήλων ἀπῳκισμέναι ταῖς κατὰ τὴν ἀνατολὴν τετραμμέναις ῥυμοτομίαις, ἐξίσου πᾶσαι τὸ σεληναῖον φῶς ὑποδέχονται. Αἷς εἰ μὴ πάσαις ἀντιπρόσωπος ἦν, τοὺς μὲν ἐπ' εὐθείας τῶν στενωπῶν πάντως ἂν κατεφώτισε, τοὺς δὲ τὸ πλάτος αὐτῆς ὑπερπίπ τοντας ἐγκεκλιμέναις ἂν ταῖς αὐγαῖς ἐπὶ τὰ πλάγια παραφερομέναις προσέβαλλεν. Ὅπερ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν λύχνων ἐστὶν ἰδεῖν κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους γινόμενον. Ἐπειδὰν πλείους περιστῶσιν αὐτὸν, ἡ μὲν τοῦ κατ' εὐθεῖαν ἑστῶτος σκιὰ πρὸς τὸ ὄρθιον ἀποτείνεται, αἱ δὲ λοιπαὶ καθ' ἑκάτερον μέρος ἐκκλίνουσιν. Ὥστε εἰ μὴ ἄπλετόν τι ἦν καὶ ὑπερέχον μεγέθει τὸ σεληνιακὸν σῶμα, οὐκ ἂν ὁμοίως ἀντιπαρετείνετο πᾶσιν. Ὁμοίως γὰρ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ τῶν ἰσημερινῶν τόπων ἀνατελλούσης οἵ τε προσοικοῦντες τῇ κατεψυγμένῃ καὶ ὑπὸ τὰς περιστροφὰς τῆς ἄρκτου κείμενοι μεταλαμβάνουσι, καὶ οἱ κατὰ τὰ κοῖλα τῆς μεσημβρίας τῆς διακεκαυμένης γείτονες· οἷς πᾶσι κατὰ τὸ πλάτος ἀντιπαρήκουσα, σαφεστάτην μαρτυρίαν τοῦ μεγέθους παρέχεται. Τίς οὖν ἀντερεῖ μὴ οὐχὶ παμμέγεθες αὐτῆς εἶναι τὸ σῶμα, τὸ τηλικούτοις ὁμοῦ καὶ τοσούτοις διαστήμασιν ἐξισούμενον; Καὶ τὰ μὲν περὶ μεγεθῶν ἡλίου καὶ σελήνης ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον. Ἡμῖν δὲ ὁ χαρισάμενος διάνοιαν ἐκ τῶν μικροτάτων τῆς κτίσεως τὴν μεγάλην τοῦ τεχνίτου σοφίαν καταμανθάνειν, παράσχοι καὶ ἐκ τῶν μεγάλων μείζονας λαμβάνειν τὰς ἐννοίας τοῦ κτίσαντος. Καίτοιγε συγκρίσει τοῦ ποιητοῦ, ἥλιος καὶ σελήνη ἐμπίδος καὶ μύρμηκος ἐπέχουσι λόγον. Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀξίαν τοῦ μεγέθους τοῦ Θεοῦ τῶν ὅλων ἐκ τούτων λαβεῖν τὴν θεωρίαν, ἀλλὰ μικραῖς τισι καὶ ἀμυδραῖς ἐμφάσεσι δι' αὐτῶν προβιβασθῆναι, ὥσπερ καὶ δι' ἑκάστου τῶν μικροτάτων ἐν ζῴοις ἢ ἐν βοτάναις. Ἀρκέσθωμεν τοῖς εἰρημένοις· ἐγὼ μὲν εὐχαριστήσας τῷ τὴν μικράν μοι ταύτην διακονίαν τοῦ λόγου χαρισαμένῳ, ὑμεῖς δὲ τῷ διατρέφοντι ὑμᾶς ταῖς πνευματικαῖς τροφαῖς, ὃς καὶ νῦν ὑμᾶς οἷον κριθίνῳ τινὶ ἄρτῳ τῇ εὐτελείᾳ τῆς ἡμετέρας φωνῆς διέθρεψε· καὶ διατρέφοι γε εἰς ἀεὶ, κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς πίστεως χαριζόμενος ὑμῖν τὴν φανέρωσιν τοῦ Πνεύματος, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
thought_title: The moon's size and the limits of human reasoning
orientation: Basil is concluding his discussion of the fourth day's lights, arguing that the moon's vast size is proven by its simultaneous visibility across distant cities, and that even the greatest heavenly bodies are small compared to God.
pass_a_gloss: But the western sea undergoes the ebb-tides, now receding, and again flooding over, as if by the respirations of the moon being drawn back, and again by the inspirations from it, being pushed forward to its own measure. These things have been said by me for demonstration of the size according to the lights, and for proof that not even up to a syllable is any of the God-inspired words idle; and yet the word has touched upon almost none of the essential points; for there are many things about the sizes and distances of sun and moon to be found out by reasonings, for the one who has not casually examined their activities and their powers. Therefore we must rightly accuse ourselves of our own weakness, so that the greatest of the created works may not be measured by our word, but from a few of the things said we may reason by ourselves, how many and how great are the things passed over. Do not then measure even the moon with the eye, but with reasoning, which is much more accurate than the eyes for the discovery of truth. Some laughable myths babbled by tipsy old women have been spread everywhere, that by certain sorceries the moon, moved from its own seat, is brought down to the earth. How then will the incantation of sorcerers move her, whom the Most High himself established? And what place would receive her when she was pulled down? Do you wish from small proofs to take the demonstration of her size? The cities throughout the inhabited world, situated very far from each other, with their street-plans turned toward the east, all equally receive the moonlight. If she were not facing all of them, she would have illuminated those in a straight line of the narrow streets entirely, but to those exceeding her breadth she would have cast her rays, being bent and carried sideways to the sides. Which thing it is also possible to see happening with lamps in houses. Whenever more people stand around it, the shadow of the one standing in a straight line extends upright, but the remaining shadows incline to each side. So that if the lunar body were not something immense and surpassing in size, it would not equally extend opposite to all. For when she rises equally from the equatorial regions, both those dwelling in the frozen zone and lying under the revolutions of the Bear share in it, and those in the hollows of the south, neighbors of the scorched zone; to all of whom, extending opposite according to breadth, she provides the clearest testimony of her size. Who then will deny that her body is not altogether huge, the body that is made equal to such great and so many distances at once? And the matters about the sizes of sun and moon, to this extent. But may he who granted us understanding to learn the great wisdom of the craftsman from the smallest things of creation, grant us also from the great things to receive greater thoughts of the Creator. And yet in comparison with the Maker, sun and moon hold the rank of a gnat and an ant. For it is not possible to take from these a contemplation worthy of the greatness of the God of all things, but to be advanced through them by certain small and dim reflections, just as also through each of the smallest things among animals or among plants. Let us be content with what has been said; I, having given thanks to him who granted me this small ministry of the word, and you, to him who nourishes you with spiritual foods, who also now nourished you as with some barley bread, by the cheapness of our voice; and may he nourish you forever, granting to you according to the proportion of faith the manifestation of the Spirit, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be the glory and the power unto the ages of ages.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the heavenly lights created on the fourth day.
Renders the compound literally as 'God-inspired' to preserve the theological force of Scripture's divine origin.

choices.term: τὴν μικράν μοι ταύτην διακονίαν τοῦ λόγου
choices.english: this small ministry of the word
choices.why: Keeps 'ministry' for διακονία to reflect Basil's humble framing of his preaching task.
rejected: this small service of the word

choices.why: Preserves the simile's humble, coarse quality; barley bread was poor man's food, matching Basil's self-deprecation.
rejected: with a kind of barley loaf
with barley bread of a sort

choices.why: Literal rendering of the tiny creatures to convey the vast disproportion between creation and Creator.
Keeps 'manifestation' for φανέρωσις, a term with Pauline resonance for the Spirit's revelatory work.

pass_b_english: The western sea, by contrast, undergoes its ebb tides, now receding and then flooding over again, as if drawn backward by the moon's exhalations and then pushed forward to its proper measure by her out-breathings. I have said these things to demonstrate the size of the lights and to establish that not even a syllable of the God-inspired words is idle. And yet my discourse has touched on almost none of the essential points. For those who have examined the workings and powers of the sun and moon with care can discover by reasoning a great deal about their sizes and distances. We ought, then, to accuse ourselves honestly of our own weakness, so that the greatest of created works are not measured by our own speech, but rather so that from the few things said we may reckon for ourselves how many and how great are the things left unmentioned.

Do not, therefore, measure even the moon with your eye, but with reasoning, which is far more accurate than the eyes for discovering truth. Some laughable myths, babbled everywhere by old women in their cups, have spread the claim that the moon is moved from her own seat by certain sorceries and brought down to the earth. How could a magician's incantation move her whom the Most High himself established? And what place could receive her if she were dragged down? Do you want to grasp the proof of her size from small indications? The cities throughout the inhabited world, though separated from one another by the greatest distances, all receive the moon's light equally in their streets turned toward the east. If she were not directly opposite them all, she would certainly illuminate those in the straight line of the narrow streets, but for those beyond her breadth she would cast her rays obliquely, slanting them to the sides. This is what one can see happening with lamps in houses. When several people stand around a lamp, the shadow of the one standing directly in front of it extends upright, while the remaining shadows incline to each side. So if the moon's body were not immense and surpassing in size, it would not extend equally opposite to all.

For when she rises from the equatorial regions, those who dwell in the frozen zone and lie beneath the turnings of the Bear receive her light just as those who live in the hollows of the south, neighbors of the scorched zone. Extending opposite to all of them across her breadth, she provides the clearest testimony of her size. Who, then, will deny that her body is enormous, matching such great and numerous distances at once? Let this suffice concerning the sizes of the sun and moon.

May he who granted us understanding to learn the great wisdom of the Craftsman from the smallest things of creation also grant us to receive from the great things even greater conceptions of the Creator. And yet, in comparison with the Maker, the sun and moon hold the rank of a gnat and an ant. For it is not possible to gain from these a vision worthy of the greatness of the God of all things, but only to be led forward by small and faint impressions through them, just as through each of the smallest things among animals or plants.

Let us be content with what has been said. I give thanks to him who granted me this small ministry of the word, and you to him who nourishes you with spiritual food—who even now has fed you, as with some barley bread, through the humble quality of our voice. And may he nourish you forever, granting you the manifestation of the Spirit according to the measure of your faith, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be glory and power forever and ever.

problems.quote: babbled everywhere by old women in their cups
problems.why: κωθωνιζομένων means 'drinking toasts/drinking deeply,' not specifically 'in their cups.' The participle describes the act of drinking, not drunkenness.
problems.fix: babbled everywhere by old women deep in their cups

problems.quote: as if drawn backward by the moon's respirations and then pushed forward to its proper measure by her inspirations
problems.source_quote: ὥσπερ ἀναπνοαῖς τῆς σελήνης ὑφελκομένη πρὸς τὸ ὀπίσω, καὶ πάλιν ταῖς ἀπ' αὐτῆς ἐμπνοίαις, εἰς τὸ οἰκεῖον μέτρον προωθουμένη
problems.why: ἀναπνοαῖς and ἐμπνοίαις are both 'breathing out/exhalations'; 'respirations' and 'inspirations' falsely suggests inhalation vs exhalation. Both are out-breathings.
problems.fix: as if drawn backward by the moon's exhalations and then pushed forward to its proper measure by her out-breathings
problems.ruling: ἀναπνοαῖς and ἐμπνοίαις both denote exhalations; 'inspirations' wrongly implies inhalation.

problems.quote: the shadow of the one standing directly in front of it stretches straight ahead
problems.source_quote: ἡ μὲν τοῦ κατ' εὐθεῖαν ἑστῶτος σκιὰ πρὸς τὸ ὄρθιον ἀποτείνεται
problems.why: πρὸς τὸ ὄρθιον means 'upright/vertically,' not 'straight ahead.' The shadow goes upward, not forward.
problems.fix: the shadow of the one standing directly in front of it extends upright
problems.ruling: πρὸς τὸ ὄρθιον means 'upright/vertically'; 'straight ahead' misstates the shadow's direction.

problems.quote: the others lean to one side or the other
problems.source_quote: αἱ δὲ λοιπαὶ καθ' ἑκάτερον μέρος ἐκκλίνουσιν
problems.why: αἱ δὲ λοιπαὶ refers to 'the remaining shadows,' not 'the others' [people]. The shadows incline, not the people.
problems.fix: while the remaining shadows incline to each side
problems.ruling: αἱ δὲ λοιπαὶ refers to shadows (σκιά), not people; 'the others' misleads the reader.

refereed.quote: as if drawn backward by the moon's exhalations and then pushed forward to its proper measure by her out-breathings
refereed.source_quote: ὥσπερ ἀναπνοαῖς τῆς σελήνης ὑφελκομένη πρὸς τὸ ὀπίσω, καὶ πάλιν ταῖς ἀπ' αὐτῆς ἐμπνοίαις, εἰς τὸ οἰκεῖον μέτρον προωθουμένη
refereed.why: Reverses agency: Greek has moon drawn back by moon's breaths, pushed forward by her in-breathings; English reverses to 'exhalations' drawing back and 'out-breathings' pushing forward.
refereed.fix: as if drawn backward by the moon's inhalations and then pushed forward to its proper measure by her exhalations
refereed.ruling: ἀναπνοαῖς (in-breaths) draws back; ἐμπνοαῖς (out-breaths) pushes forward. English reverses both, changing the analogy's meaning.
